audit_status.source_base: ChatGPT-authored Psalms completion draft using public-domain KJV as familiar alignment scaffold with curated Hebrew/textual overrides; full WLC/OSHB/source-witness audit pending
audit_status.review_note: Songs of Ascents, lying speech, conflict, Meshech/Kedar imagery, peace, and war.

verses.restored: In my distress I cried to YHWH, and he heard me.

familiar.text: In my distress I cried unto the LORD, and he heard me.

notes.title: Songs of Ascents begin
notes.body: Psalm 120 begins the collection of Songs of Ascents (Psalms 120–134), likely associated in some way with pilgrimage or ascent, though the precise historical use is debated.

modern.text: In my distress I cried to the LORD, and He answered me.

original.text: שִׁ֗יר הַֽמַּ֫עֲל֥וֹת אֶל יְ֭הוָה בַּצָּרָ֣תָה לִּ֑י קָ֝רָ֗אתִי וַֽיַּעֲנֵֽנִי

verses.restored: YHWH, rescue my life from lying lips and from a deceitful tongue.

familiar.text: Deliver my soul, O LORD, from lying lips, and from a deceitful tongue.

modern.text: Deliver my soul, O LORD, from lying lips and a deceitful tongue.

original.text: יְֽהוָ֗ה הַצִּ֣ילָה נַ֭פְשִׁי מִשְּׂפַת שֶׁ֑קֶר מִלָּשׁ֥וֹן רְמִיָּֽה

verses.restored: What shall be given to thee? or what shall be done to thee, thou false tongue?

familiar.text: What shall be given unto thee? or what shall be done unto thee, thou false tongue?

modern.text: What will He do to you, and what will be added to you, O deceitful tongue?

original.text: מַה יִּתֵּ֣ן לְ֭ךָ וּמַה יֹּסִ֥יף לָ֗ךְ לָשׁ֥וֹן רְמִיָּֽה

verses.restored: Sharp arrows of the mighty, with coals of juniper.

familiar.text: Sharp arrows of the mighty, with coals of juniper.

modern.text: Sharp arrows will come from the warrior, with burning coals of the broom tree!

original.text: חִצֵּ֣י גִבּ֣וֹר שְׁנוּנִ֑ים עִ֝֗ם גַּחֲלֵ֥י רְתָמִֽים

verses.restored: Woe is me, that I sojourn in Mesech, that I dwell in the tents of Kedar!

familiar.text: Woe is me, that I sojourn in Mesech, that I dwell in the tents of Kedar!

modern.text: Woe to me that I dwell in Meshech, that I live among the tents of Kedar!

original.text: אֽוֹיָה לִ֭י כִּי גַ֣רְתִּי מֶ֑שֶׁךְ שָׁ֝כַ֗נְתִּי עִֽם אָהֳלֵ֥י קֵדָֽר

verses.restored: My soul hath long dwelt with him that hateth peace.

familiar.text: My soul hath long dwelt with him that hateth peace.

modern.text: Too long have I dwelt among those who hate peace.

original.text: רַ֭בַּת שָֽׁכְנָה לָּ֣הּ נַפְשִׁ֑י עִ֝֗ם שׂוֹנֵ֥א שָׁלֽוֹם

verses.restored: I am for peace: but when I speak, they are for war.

familiar.text: I am for peace: but when I speak, they are for war.

modern.text: I am in favor of peace; but when I speak, they want war.

original.text: אֲֽנִי שָׁ֭לוֹם וְכִ֣י אֲדַבֵּ֑ר הֵ֝֗מָּה לַמִּלְחָמָֽה

translation_notes: This chapter completes corpus coverage as a ChatGPT-authored draft. KJV is retained as a familiar comparison layer; a separate automated reference pass adds BSB and pointed Hebrew without replacing the restored draft.
safety_note: Ancient place/people names are poetic geography and must not become labels for modern enemies; the speaker desires peace rather than violence.
source_witness_audit_flags: Compare directly with WLC/OSHB, Septuagint, Dead Sea Psalms witnesses where extant, and other textual witnesses during the global audit. Preserve poetic parallelism, superscriptions, acrostic structure, duplicate/reused psalms, and significant Hebrew/Greek divergences rather than harmonizing them.
